sources.title: AFI Catalog: West Side Story (1961)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected cast, singing-double notes, award history and later-remake note.
supports: Natalie Wood is credited as Maria in the 1961 film.
Marni Nixon dubbed Natalie Wood's singing voice, a distinct credit from portraying Maria on screen.
AFI identifies the 2021 remake's Maria as Rachel Zegler and Rita Moreno's new role as Valentina.
limits: The dubbing note does not make Nixon the actor who played Maria in the 1961 film.
The 2021 remake is a different film and must not be used for the 1961 answer.

source_link.title: AFI Catalog: «Вестсайдская история» (1961)
source_link.supports: Подтверждает Натали Вуд — Марию, вокальный дубляж Марни Никсон и различие с фильмом 2021 года.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy: West Side Story (1961)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected role, premise, stage-musical source and award context.
supports: The Academy identifies Maria as Natalie Wood and Tony as Richard Beymer.
It describes the film as a screen version of the Broadway musical, with Laurents, Bernstein, Sondheim and Robbins credited in its creation.
It records ten Oscars, including Directing and Best Picture.
limits: The event overview is not a full cast-credit ledger for every performer.
The award count does not establish an acting Oscar for Wood.

source_link.title: Academy: «Вестсайдская история» (1961)
source_link.supports: Подтверждает Вуд как Марию, сюжетный конфликт, бродвейский источник и десять «Оскаров».

sources.title: AFI Catalog: Rebel Without a Cause (1955)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected cast, structure, production history and camera notes.
supports: James Dean is credited as Jim Stark.
The story spans twenty-four hours, and Ray used partitions to frame Jim, Judy and Plato together in the police-station scene.
The production shifted from the early Lindner case-history source toward a fictional story about teenage discontent and isolation.
limits: Jim and the completed plot are fictional and should not be presented as Lindner's real case.
The history of early unused scripts does not prove a direct one-to-one adaptation.

source_link.title: AFI Catalog: «Бунтарь без причины» (1955)
source_link.supports: Подтверждает Джеймс Дин — Джим Старк, суточную структуру, кадрирование и историю замысла.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy collection highlights: James Dean
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected biographical scope and Rebel-specific collection materials.
supports: The Academy lists Rebel without a Cause among Dean's three films before his 1955 death.
The collection includes Rebel material on Nicholas Ray, Natalie Wood, Griffith Observatory, locations and Production Code revisions.
limits: This collection overview does not itself assign a character credit or diagnose Jim Stark.
Its phrase that Dean's latter two films earned Oscar nominations conflicts with the Academy's 1956 and 1957 ceremony ledgers and must not support a Rebel nomination claim.
Dean's biographical history is distinct from the fictional character.

source_link.supports: Подтверждает место фильма в короткой фильмографии Дина и архивные материалы о его создании.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy: The 28th Academy Awards (1956)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected Actor and Rebel without a Cause nomination listings.
supports: James Dean is listed as an Actor nominee for East of Eden.
Rebel without a Cause is listed with nominations for Sal Mineo, Natalie Wood and Nicholas Ray.
limits: The 1956 ceremony honors 1955 releases.
The ledger does not list James Dean as a nominee for Rebel without a Cause.

source_link.supports: Подтверждает номинацию Дина за «К востоку от рая» и номинации «Бунтаря без причины» без Дина.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy: The 29th Academy Awards (1957)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected Actor nomination listing.
supports: James Dean is listed as an Actor nominee for Giant.
limits: The 1957 ceremony honors 1956 releases.
This ledger is award evidence only, not a source for Jim Stark's role or the film's plot.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: Psycho (1960)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected cast, literary source, title design and adaptation notes.
supports: Anthony Perkins is credited as Norman Bates.
The film is based on Robert Bloch's 1959 novel Psycho.
AFI describes Saul Bass's divided-line title design and says the film rewrote novel-Norman as younger and more vulnerable with Perkins cast.
limits: Norman is fictional; adaptation discussion is not clinical diagnosis.
AFI's note on Ed Gein concerns a partial inspiration for Bloch's novel, not a claim that the film recounts real events.

source_link.supports: Подтверждает Энтони Перкинс — Нормана Бейтса, роман Блоха как источник и решения титров/адаптации.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy collection highlights: Alfred Hitchcock
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected Academy's Hitchcock career context for Psycho.
supports: The Academy places Psycho in Hitchcock's 1958–63 run of influential films.
It calls Psycho Hitchcock's first turn to full-blooded horror.
It says Psycho pushed viewers' nerves, censorship boundaries and advertising practice.
limits: This career overview does not establish the actor-to-role credit; AFI supplies that credit.
Its broad critical framing should not be converted into medical claims about characters.

source_link.title: Academy: материалы коллекции об Альфреде Хичкоке
source_link.supports: Подтверждает место «Психо» в творческом периоде Хичкока и контекст хоррора, цензуры и рекламы.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: The Maltese Falcon (1941)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected cast, literary source, adaptation history and awards note.
supports: Humphrey Bogart is credited as Samuel Spade, while John Huston is credited as director and screenwriter.
The film is based on Dashiell Hammett's 1930 novel.
Warner Bros. had made earlier 1931 and 1936 screen adaptations of the Hammett story; AFI also records 1941 nominations for Sydney Greenstreet, Huston and the picture.
limits: The 1941 film is a distinct adaptation, not the first or sole screen version of Hammett's story.
The falcon's legend and the detective story are fictional narrative material.

source_link.supports: Подтверждает Хамфри Богарт — Сэм Спейд, роман Хэммета и различие с экранизациями 1931 и 1936 годов.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy press release: Bogart Double Bill Featured for Academy Standard Screenings
sources.access_method: Direct web open of Academy PDF; inspected the Maltese Falcon listing and its nominations.
supports: The Academy describes the film as directed by John Huston and starring Humphrey Bogart.
It lists Mary Astor, Sydney Greenstreet and Peter Lorre among Bogart's co-stars.
It records Greenstreet's supporting-actor nomination and Huston's screenplay nomination.
limits: The 1993 screening release is historical collection context, not a full production record.
It does not establish the novel's adaptation history; AFI supplies that distinction.
